frictions: Fast-mode port blocked before any code changed: 2 of 4 items (per-file failure isolation, honest partial results on timeout) have no red-then-green test path. Lsp_client.t is abstract with no constructor but `start` (spawns a real server), extract_symbols takes it, and the repo has no LSP integration harness.
Measured asymmetry: the CMT producer has 69 tezt tests; the LSP producer has 0. The untestability is not local to these two fixes, it is the state of that half of the library.
Lsp_extractor is not re-exported in arch_index.mli, so even the pure helpers (file_uri_of_path, relative_path, scan_source_files) are unreachable from test/ without a surface addition.
methods: identifier-level inventory across the two forks before scoping (19 epure-only identifiers, only 4 crossing)
checked for an injection seam and an integration harness before declaring the items untestable, rather than assuming
suggestion: roster-run's Fast/Full classifier asks 'what to build vs how'. A third question would have caught this earlier: 'can each change be proven by a test that fails first?' An unprovable change in Fast mode is a Full-mode design question about testability, not an implementation detail.

frictions: The skill's questions.md template mandates '# Research Questions — <task-slug>' while the same skill requires zero intent disclosure. For a descriptive slug (here: port-fork-robustness-fixes) the title briefs the blind researcher on exactly what the file exists to hide. Deviated deliberately and recorded the reason in the file itself.
methods: greped the produced questions for goal vocabulary before presenting them, rather than trusting the generator to have stayed neutral — 4 hits, 3 were regex noise (re-exported, transport, fixture) and 1 was the mandated title
suggestion: Either drop the slug from the questions.md title, or have roster-question derive a neutral title from the domain (e.g. '# Research Questions — language-server extraction') while the filename keeps the slug. The filename is not read by the researcher; the title is.

frictions: The scoping inventory compared the two forks by IDENTIFIER, not by behaviour: it grepped for `partial_fns` (a name chosen in the other codebase) and read its absence as the absence of honest-partial-results, which this repo already implements as `fn_rows_ref`. Two of four items evaporated on first contact with the code.

A grep for 'ocamllsp|run_lsp|OCAMLLSP' over test/ tezt/ returned nothing and was read as 'no LSP test harness exists'. The harness exists (tezt/tests/lsp_readiness.ml) — a STUB server does not mention ocamllsp, and it drives the CLI binary rather than run_lsp. Third absence-from-a-bounded-search in one session.

The first version of the diagnostics test asserted the sentinel appeared SOMEWHERE in the output. The stub refuses every request, so a second site surfaced the same sentinel and the mutation removing the first diagnostic SURVIVED. The test passed for the wrong reason and would have shipped as proof.
methods: red observed before every fix, with the exit code recorded, not asserted
every mutation run through `dune test` rather than by invoking a test binary — the shortcut that invalidated a mutation table earlier this week
reused the repo's own stub-server pattern instead of designing a seam, once research found it
suggestion: roster-question/research should carry an explicit instruction to compare BEHAVIOUR across forks, not identifiers — 'grep the name' is the default move and it is wrong whenever the two sides were written by different hands. A one-line rule in roster-research ('an identifier's absence is not a behaviour's absence; find the behaviour') would have saved this task two phases.

frictions: Both available secondary runtimes degraded with reason=tree-mutation, runtime_exit=3, on the same prompt (digest f351472844ff5fea). codex applied the M1 mutation from the brief's mutation table (removing the absolutisation in file_uri_of_path); opencode deleted 9 lines from lsp_extractor.ml, i.e. one of the new diagnostics. Neither reported a finding. So the mandatory cross-runtime pass is structurally unavailable here, not merely flaky: 2 of 2 runtimes reproduce the experiments described in the prompt instead of reporting observations about them.

Hypothesis worth testing before blaming the runtimes: the prompt embeds the impl brief, which contains a mutation table naming exact code edits (M1..M5). A runtime given write access and a list of mutations may reasonably read it as work to perform. The wrapper's tree-integrity snapshot caught it both times, which is the safeguard working.
methods: restored the tree after each degraded run and verified `git diff HEAD --stat` was empty before continuing, rather than trusting the wrapper's cleanup
inspected what each runtime mutated before discarding its output — the mutation itself is information even when the findings are void
suggestion: xruntime-review should either strip mutation-table-like sections from the prompt it forwards, or state in the forwarded prompt that the runtime has read-only intent and any edit voids the run. Right now the prompt hands a runtime an explicit list of code edits and then fails it for making them.

frictions: Four review rounds, every one finding something real. The recurring class was never the code and never the intent — it was a claim about coverage that the coverage did not support. Round 2's was the sharpest: a scripted edit whose anchor no longer matched, and Python silently does nothing when the pattern is absent, so the brief asserted a fix with byte-identical code behind it.

Round 3's fix (report_once) shipped with zero coverage because the existing stub refuses EVERY request, so documentSymbol fails, no functions are extracted, and the site under test is never reached. A stub that is too aggressive is indistinguishable from a stub that works, and the test still passes.

QA's first pass NO-GO'd on a missing library, having run in the default opam switch. It escalated an environment diagnosis into a verdict on the branch, and explicitly disbelieved a measurement I had taken correctly.

Reported a copyright gate as passing when the script does not exist in this repo — the exit code came from tail inside a pipe. Third instance this session of reading an exit code from the wrong process.
methods: Mutation as the unit of proof: 21 mutants, 20 killed, each run through the command the report cites. The one survivor is documented as a survivor.
Assert the anchor of every scripted edit. One assertion fired and caught a no-op edit.
Counts, not containments, whenever the property IS the number. contains cannot tell 3 from 126.
Bound a delta by what CANNOT have changed: 3292 edges outside the touched file were raw-byte-identical, which bounds the golden's +2 without trusting any normalisation.
Verify at production scale, not only on the fixture: 91 diagnostics across 91 files on 2603 functions, where the fixture only ever showed 3 on 3.
suggestion: roster-qa should hard-verify its toolchain before running any gate, and be forbidden from returning NO-GO on a missing-dependency error without first printing proof that the environment was right. A missing library is an environment diagnosis, not a verdict on a branch — and an agent that converts one into the other produces exactly the false red that trains people to bypass gates.

frictions: round-1 baseline recalibration was measured on the ambient (dirty) working tree instead of a clean checkout, caught only by review — every future numeric-baseline ratchet in this repo should measure from git worktree add --detach from the start
methods: fixed all review findings directly rather than re-delegating to a sub-agent, since round 2 was a small, well-scoped diff
verified the exit-code contract fix live by removing sqlite3 from PATH and confirming exit 2, not just reading the try/catch
wrote and red/green-verified a new ratchet check for the one HIGH finding that needed one per the loop-back ratchet rule
suggestion: the review skill could recommend measuring any numeric baseline from a clean worktree by default, given this is the second time in this repo a dirty-tree measurement produced a wrong number (see also the 475-rejected-rows figure from the divergence branch mentioned in the roadmap)

frictions: the convergence gate correctly refused a check_encodable:false HIGH finding without an explicit human ACCEPT even after independent re-verification of the fix — a good guardrail, but meant a second AskUserQuestion round for what felt like a formality; the gate never takes a reviewer's own verification as a substitute for ACCEPT

forgot to set pre_fix_sha on round-1 HIGH findings at NO-GO time; the gate did not catch this until round 2 (it only checks pre_fix_sha validity when resolving a check-linked finding, not at NO-GO emission) — worth setting this field immediately when drafting any NO-GO with new HIGH+ findings
methods: delta-scoped specialist re-selection on the loop-back round: only reviewer (always) and architect (named on OPEN findings) re-ran, not a full fan-out, per the skill's own round>=2 selection rule

cross-checked every claimed fix against actual file content and a live re-run (removed sqlite3 from PATH to confirm exit 2, rebuilt in a fresh clean worktree to confirm the recalibrated number) rather than trusting the diff alone
suggestion: a lightweight lint on review.json drafts checking pre_fix_sha is set and full-length for every HIGH+ finding the moment it is written, not only at gate time, would have caught the missing-field issue a round earlier
